text:
mia: FYI noticed a cluster in us-west2 with repeated ECC+Xid bursts + short network flaps, nodes not fully failing but pods are getting OOM-ish stalls. Thought we should discuss whether to evacuate earlier than our current 5-min hysteresis.
sanjay: Can you paste the alert pattern? Is it ECC-only or combined with net.kern drops?
mia: ECC spikes (30-40/sec for ~20s), then a flurry of TCP retransmits and kube-proxy errors. infra-bot: [alert] gpu-ecc-spike us-west2-gpu-pool-3 node=gpu-12 count=38 window=22s severity=high
ashley: Sounds like the flaky-card pattern we've seen, but this one also shows NIC flakiness. If we only cordon on ECC we might leave pods stuck with partial network.
julio: Are we able to detect simultaneous health signals and treat as accelerated evacuation? current policy: if gpu.xid>=10 within 60s -> soft-cordon; if persists 5m -> drain.
mia: Right. Proposed tweak: if ECC_rate>25/s AND net_retrans>500 in 30s, escalate to immediate soft-evac (cordon + annotation) and schedule drain after 60s unless metrics recover. That avoids long-running stuck inference streams.
sanjay: I worry about churn and cost — immediate drains will push jobs to other regions and spike preemptible usage. Can we add cost-aware routing: if pod tolerates CPU fallback, reschedule to cpu-backfill class first before cross-region?
ashley: Good idea. Policy sketch: 1) immediate cordon + annotate:reason=multi-signal 2) attempt local node-local fallback: taint:effect=PreferNoSchedule to allow CPU-only resched 3) if pods have toleration cpu-fallback=true -> move in-cluster; else drain to remote pool after 60s.
julio: Implementation notes: kubectl commands for manual repro: ```kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl annotate node/gpu-12 evacuation=multi-signal && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force``` We'll need to wrap in controller to avoid force kills on stateful jobs (slurm nodes behave differently).
mia: For slurm nodes runbook: `scontrol setnode gpu-12 state=DRAIN Reason="multi-signal-evac"` then trigger procd that migrates running jobs to the preemption queue.
sanjay: Could the autoscaler be taught to hold capacity in-region when these accelerations happen? e.g., keep a 10% buffer for hot spares.
nashley: We're already at reserved headroom for p99 loads, but hot-spare policy could be dynamic: increase local reserve for 10m after N hard-evacuations in 1h. adds cost but reduces cross-region egress.
infra-bot: [proposal created] multi-signal-evac-policy PR#274 details at https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/274 : includes k8s controller + slurm hook + cost-buffer toggle.
mia: Can oncall run a simulated test on staging? I'd like to see behavior when NIC error bounces back quickly vs persistent.
oncall-rotations: I can run a canary tomorrow at 0300 UTC; will validate no surprise mass-drain.
sanjay: Add a cooldown: if a node recovered after cordon within 90s, uncordon automatically; only escalate if repeated within 15m. That should cut false positives.
note: reactions: :thumbsup: from ashley, :eyes: from julio
mia: Also add telemetry: sample pre/post-token-latency, eviction counts, and cross-region egress bytes. We'll tie alerts to cost dashboards so PMs can see impact.
nashley: I'll open the config PR for the controller and add a feature flag behind remote:evac.experimental=true. Keep default off for now.
sanjay: Sounds good. Thanks all.
